Same suggestion as above (`on?.map`) if that's fine with you all.

That code has always been so hard to read—it scares me every time haha. Not sure if that's just me. If not, it'd be nice to rethink why it's been made like that.

Either way is fine to me for this line though.

Not sure you're aware but we plan long-term to remove the `init` step and solely rely on `render`. Looking forward to this time—it'll remove all the conditional logic so we can focus on a single contained behavior.

I've already wrote a suite of RFC ([Request For Comments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Request_for_Comments), kind of proposal + specs) if ever it's of interest, there's a bunch of stuff I learned experimenting on this, so you might too!

It's a 3-part series:

- [Render Lifecycle: Schedule Renders (1/3)](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch-rfcs/pull/28)
- [Render Lifecycle: Run Effects (2/3)](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch-rfcs/pull/29)
- [Render Lifecycle: Memoize Renders (3/3) ](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch-rfcs/pull/30)

It might be the next simplification that we bring to InstantSearch?

I can't seem to find a good solution for now, It's either **duplicate code with separated blocs** (which is easier to read) or **remove duplicated logic but add conditional logic/complexity** (which is harder to read but with less duplications).
